key_insight: Simple semantic and visibility priors can significantly improve lidar semantic scene completion without making the model architecture more complex. The paper shows that carefully chosen, possibly noisy, auxiliary cues can boost performance as effectively as heavier redesigns.
problem_solved: Existing lidar semantic scene completion methods often rely on increasingly complex architectures, which raises model size and training complexity. This paper addresses how to improve SSC performance using lightweight, easy-to-add priors instead of major network changes.
method: Explore semantic priors to inject class-level information into the SSC pipeline.
Use visibility priors to help the model reason about which regions are observed versus occluded.
Treat these priors as simple auxiliary inputs or ingredients that enhance existing SSC networks with minimal architectural changes.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical path to better performance without the cost of redesigning or scaling up models. It is especially useful when computational efficiency, simplicity, and ease of integration matter.
visual_elements: Before/after pipeline diagram showing a baseline SSC model versus the same model augmented with priors

A performance lift bar chart comparing baseline and prior-enhanced results

paper_title: SSC-Priors: Exploring Semantic and Visibility Priors to Boost Lidar Semantic Scene Completion
paper_authors: Tetiana Martyniuk, Jonathan Seele, Alexandre Boulch, Gilles Puy, Renaud Marlet
